patient.name: Maya Ellis
patient.weightNote: V1: weight is narrative-only; the engine runs 80 kg adult physiology for every patient.

dispatch.cadText: Caller says wife is passed out on the bathroom floor and barely breathing. Says she maybe had a seizure or maybe just fell asleep. Not sure if she was drinking. Door was locked and he had to push it open a few minutes ago.
updates: Caller is crying and hard to understand, staying with her in bathroom

scene.description: Small home bathroom in afternoon light. Young woman on floor by toilet. Pill bottles on the counter, one with another name on label. Tight space with little room to work.

backstory: She is limp and barely responsive and drifts in and out. She mumbles a few slurred words when shaken loudly then goes quiet again. Her breathing looks slow and shallow and she does not push you away.
conditionsNote: Dispatch Engine v1: generatorReady conditions only; see skeleton.

bystander.label: Panicked spouse
bystander.notes: Hovers, cries, answers in fragments, needs one clear job or keeps crowding your workspace.

persona: She is limp and barely responsive and drifts in and out. She mumbles a few slurred words when shaken loudly then goes quiet again. Her breathing looks slow and shallow and she does not push you away.

SAMPLE.signs_symptoms: Very sleepy, hard to wake, slow shallow breathing, nausea earlier per spouse
SAMPLE.medications: No home meds on file, no daily pills she admits to
SAMPLE.past_history: No known medical problems reported, prior low mood per spouse
SAMPLE.last_meal: Ate lunch earlier, time unclear, spouse unsure
SAMPLE.events: Found in locked bathroom after being quiet a while, empty pill bottles nearby

OPQRST.onset: Found a short while ago after she went to bathroom and did not come out
OPQRST.provokes: Loud voice and sternal rub briefly wake her, quiet lets her fade again
OPQRST.quality: Drowsy mumbling, heavy limbs, sick to stomach feeling
OPQRST.radiates: No pain complaint, just feels heavy and foggy when roused
OPQRST.severity_words: Worst drowsiness she has ever felt, cannot stay awake
OPQRST.time: Symptoms ongoing since found, getting sleepier per spouse

secrets.fact: Pills were prescription pain tablets belonging to a relative, not prescribed to her
secrets.revealWhen: Asked whose name is on the bottle or where pills came from?

secrets.fact: Took extra tablets after argument because she wanted to sleep and stop stress
secrets.revealWhen: Asked why she took them or what happened today?

bystanderLines: Please please wake up - baby please - do something!
I - I knocked and knocked - the door was locked - I pushed - I...
expectedPathway: Ensure scene safety and open space to work, assign spouse one clear job away from patient. Assess responsiveness and airway with breathing support as needed. Recognize opioid toxidrome from story and pill bottles, support ventilation with oxygen per protocol. Give naloxone per protocol and watch for waking or re-sedation. Monitor airway closely, place in recovery position if remains sleepy, transport for ongoing care and mental health follow up.
